summary:
## 2.12.1 (2026-11-12)

This release casts all 2D lidars of a step in one batched pass, lets ORCA groups avoid the obstacles around them, and keeps lidar and collision checks in step with objects moved by hand.

Measured headless on one CPU core of a Linux machine against 2.12.0 (median step time, mean of two runs):

| Time cost | 2.12.0 | 2.12.1 | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `env.step()`, 1000 robots with 64-beam lidar (`usage/27thousand_robot_world`) | 2211 ms | 143.9 ms | 15.4x |
| `env.step()`, 1000 robots with 64-beam lidar, `ir-sim[fast]` (numba) | 2211 ms | 82.9 ms | 26.7x |
| `env.step()`, 1000 dash robots | 79.4 ms | 24.7 ms | 3.2x |
| `env.step()`, 1000 robots with explicit-ID actions | 50.1 ms | 21.6 ms | 2.3x |

### Features and Performance

- **Batched 2D lidar is up to 26.7× faster.** All `lidar2d` sensors are cast together in one pass per step, and each scan matches a single sensor's scan bit for bit. `pip install ir-sim[fast]` installs numba, which compiles the lidar cast for extra speed. See [`usage/27thousand__robot_world`](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/tree/main/usage/27thousand__robot_world) for details. ([#392](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/392))
- **ORCA groups avoid walls, grid maps and moving obstacles.** Static objects around the group, including occupied grid-map cells, enter ORCA as obstacles and moving ones as agents, so members no longer pass through them. See [`usage/19orca_world`](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/tree/main/usage/19orca_world) for details. ([#390](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/390))
- **Dash behavior is 3.2× faster for 1000 robots.** Dash robots no longer collect the list of all other objects every step, which they never used. Trajectories are unchanged. ([#389](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/389), based on [#386](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/386)) (@KataDavidXD)
- **Explicit-ID actions are 2.3× faster for 1000 robots.** `env.step(action, action_id=...)` finds each object through a lookup table instead of searching the object list once per ID. Trajectories are unchanged. ([#389](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/389), based on [#386](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/386)) (@KataDavidXD)

### Fix

- **Lidar and collision checks immediately see objects moved between environment steps.** Before, objects moved with `set_state()` or `robot.step()` were still searched at their old places until the next `env.step()`; now the geometry tree is rebuilt at the next query. ([#393](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/393))
- **GUI backend selection respects user settings and installed toolkits.** IR-SIM no longer forces a backend: `MPLBACKEND` and `matplotlib.use()` are preserved, and Matplotlib can discover Qt6 and GTK backends as well as Tk. ([#388](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/388))
- **Image-map tests clean up temporary PNG files on Windows.** Four tests no longer fail with `PermissionError` after their assertions pass. ([#383](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/383)) (@dhyey-gosa)
- **Smaller fixes.** Missing GUI toolkits produce an installation hint, and lidar range calculations no longer depend on BLAS matrix-size rounding. ([#388](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/388), [#392](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/392))

### Refactor

- **Group behaviors share `target_roles` filtering.** ORCA and SFM groups now default to `'obstacle'`; set `target_roles: all` to include robots outside the group. ([#390](https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/390))

## New Contributors
* @dhyey-gosa made their first contribution in https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/383
* @KataDavidXD made their first contribution in https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/389 https://github.com/hanruihua/ir-sim/pull/386

## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.211 speeds up compiled SAM image encoding and expands model deployment options, with additional gains and fixes across training, OCR, and exports.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **Faster compiled SAM 3 and SAM 3.1:** The image encoders run **7–9% faster** in the tested `torch.compile` setup. The optimization is specific to compiled execution; eager-mode results remain unchanged.
- 📦 **Static INT8 export for ExecuTorch:** Models can now be exported in a smaller INT8 format with calibration data. Detection, segmentation, pose, and oriented-box heads remain in FP32 to help preserve prediction quality.
- 📝 **Faster OCR on NVIDIA GPUs:** OCR can use a cached FP16 TensorRT engine, which the release reports is about **2.5× faster than ONNX Runtime on dense pages** after its initial engine build. The OCR guide also clarifies which writing systems the default recognizer supports.
- ⚡ **Faster deterministic training:** Semantic segmentation and depth workloads use a faster resizing path when deterministic mode is enabled; measured speedups reached **3.9×** for one semantic segmentation setup.
- ⚖️ **Class weighting for classification:** The `cls_pw` training option now accounts for class imbalance in classification datasets, as well as detection.
- 🖥️ **Faster CPU pooling:** SPPF uses an equivalent pooling approach on CPU, reducing measured block latency by **22–45%** without changing GPU or exported-model behavior.
- 🛠️ **Export and input fixes:** TensorRT INT8 keeps additional sensitive head layers in floating point; legacy CoreML INT8 exports are fixed; and fixes address Tiger-Pose keypoint flips and classification on float NumPy inputs.
- 📚 **Platform and documentation updates:** Guides now cover items such as PDF prediction uploads, crowded prediction results, stopped-deployment metrics, dataset cloning limits, and PP-OCRv6 language coverage.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Compiled SAM users can process images faster without changing the eager-mode path.
- ExecuTorch users gain a smaller deployment option, while keeping important prediction heads at higher precision.
- OCR users on NVIDIA GPUs can reduce recognition time on dense pages, while users of unsupported scripts are less likely to mistake detections for accurate text recognition.
- Training and CPU inference improvements can reduce run time for relevant workloads; actual gains depend on the device, model, and settings.
- Export and input fixes improve reliability when preparing models for TensorRT, CoreML, and other deployment workflows.

## What's Changed
* Fix broken RT-DETR TensorRT 10 INT8 engines and keep all head output layers in float like QAT by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26220
* Speed up SPPF on CPU with separable max pooling by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26082
* Run the PP-OCRv6 recognizer as a cached FP16 TensorRT engine by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27143
* Platform docs: Clone Images is the visitor's route; owners copy and paste by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27144
* Platform docs: Predict tab PDFs and dense results, clone model limit, stopped deployment metrics, Gemini 4 Carbon by @pderrenger in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27145
* docs: include language and character support for PP-OCRv6 by @onuralpszr in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27155
* Let CPU CI runners save and restore zstd-compressed Actions caches by @fcakyon in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27156
* Add static INT8 quantization to ExecuTorch export by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27150
* Apply cls_pw class weights to classification training by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27148
* Speed up semantic and depth training up to 3.9x under deterministic mode by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27154
* Show which languages YOLO OCR can read (Cyrillic is not supported yet) by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27157
* Fix Tiger-Pose flips and classification predict on float NumPy arrays by @sohailshk in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27146
* Fix legacy CoreML INT8 weight quantization by @amanharshx in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27131
* Encode images up to 9% faster with compiled SAM 3 by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27158


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.210...v8.4.211

**Changes:**
fix(signal): use system OpenBLAS on Windows for the eigenvalue feature (#2530)

openblas-src rejects its static build on Windows ("Non-vcpkg builds are
not supported on Windows"), so a default-feature build of
wifi-densepose-signal could not compile there. Declare ndarray-linalg
per target: openblas-system on Windows, openblas-static elsewhere. Both
stay optional, so --no-default-features still drops BLAS entirely.

Ported from #825 by @PretaxE63, keeping the dependency optional (the
original made it unconditional, which re-added BLAS to every
default-features = false consumer) and dropping an unrelated
regenerated Tauri schema.

summary:
Source snapshot validated by the CI pipeline. This entry does not contain firmware bundles.

**Changes:**
fix(train): tch-backend rpath build.rs, unreachable gaussian-peak test thresholds, --val-dir and --eval-only (#1014) (#1014)

Rebased residual of #1014 onto main. The tch 0.24 compile fixes, clamp_min,
floor-division decode and E0507 test fix from the original PR already landed
on main (#1008 / ADR-155), so only what main still lacks is carried here:

- build.rs: with `tch-backend` + LIBTORCH_USE_PYTORCH=1, embed an rpath to
  the PyTorch lib dir. On main the lib unit-test binary dies at load with
  "libtorch_cpu.so: cannot open shared object file". Strict no-op unless the
  feature AND the env var are set (default / --no-default-features / wheel
  builds unchanged). Honours PYTHON_SYS_EXECUTABLE like torch-sys.
- losses.rs: two gaussian-peak tests asserted values that are mathematically
  unreachable for a half-pixel keypoint: exp(-0.5/8) = 0.9394 (< 0.95) and
  exp(-0.5/4.5) = 0.8948 (< 0.9). Thresholds 0.93 / 0.89 with the math.
- trainer.rs: evaluate() and new evaluate_with_dump() share ONE loop
  (evaluate_inner with an optional JSONL sink), so --eval-only measures with
  exactly the metric training validation uses.
- train.rs: --val-dir <DIR> uses a held-out MM-Fi dir as validation, taking
  precedence over the automatic subject-disjoint split; any subject overlap
  with --data-dir is refused as a leak (ADR-155 Tier-1.2). The automatic
  split and the synthetic smoke-test fallback are unchanged.
  --eval-only --checkpoint <FILE> --val-dir <DIR> [--dump-preds <JSONL>]
  loads a checkpoint and runs the validation loop standalone.

Local evidence (PyTorch 2.11, LIBTORCH_USE_PYTORCH=1, --test-threads=1):
main 353 pass / 2 fail (+ loader error without LD_LIBRARY_PATH);
this branch 355/355 with no LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

Co-authored-by: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>
